newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Malbak confirms motor subsidiary sale.
newsitem.headline: Malbak confirms motor subsidiary sale.

text.p: Malbak Ltd confirmed on Monday that Sankorp Ltd had bought its subsidiary Malbak Motor Holdings (MMH) in a transaction valued at 265 million rand.
Malbak said in a statement that agreement had been reached between the two parties late last week and that the transaction was effective retrospectively from March 1.

This forms part of the Malbak group's unbundling whereby it is disposing of its unlisted investments. Malbak plans to distribute the sale proceeds to its shareholders in cash at the same time as distributing shares in its listed subsidiaries.
Sankorp, which will be paying cash for the purchase, has not yet outlined its intentions for the motor group which achieved sales of 3.2 billion rand in the year ended August 31, 1996.

"The group has a well spread portfolio of marques and competent management who have experience of the difficult trading conditions the motor industry is currency going through," said Sankorp director Tony Routledge.
"We are confident that MMH will make a growing contribution to Sankorp's bottom line."

In a separate announcement on Monday Scaw Metals, a division of Amic Industries Ltd, said it had agreed to buy a further 16 percent stake in Haggie Ltd from Malbak at a purchase price of 25 rand a share.
Malbak's remaining 20 percent stake in Haggie will be distributed pro-rata to its shareholders on the basis of 1.24 Haggie shares for every 100 Malbak shares held.
